correctness.rationale: The DRAFT deduction is logically valid as a lemma: for integer s>=0 the Sobolev norm contains the L2 term so H^s continuously embeds in L2; the Bergman projection P is by definition the L2 orthogonal projection onto closed subspace A2, hence Pf=f in L2 for every holomorphic L2 function; a nonzero holomorphic H^s function is thus fixed with identical H^s norm, quotient exactly 1 (0/0 excluded). Constants witness non-vacuity on a bounded domain. No kernel asymptotics or worm geometry is used. This is proof, not experiment, and each step checks out.

originality.rationale: The headline disproof claim that Pf=f and the H^s quotient is 1 on holomorphic data is the textbook definition of the Bergman projection restated. Every standard source (Barrett 1992 preliminaries, Krantz Function Theory of Several Complex Variables, D'Angelo, Chen-Shaw) defines P as the L2 orthogonal projection onto A2 and states reproduction on A2. A timestamp or failed live search does not establish priority; substantively the submitted headline is immediately implied by that definition without any new argument, computation, or extension. Hence no original contribution. Live retrieval was attempted and reported total outage, but definitional textbook status does not depend on it.
